title: Scoped memory for Spaces, Projects and named agents with isolation
summary: Give agent_memory an explicit scope kind and id (user, space, project, agent), filter recall by the active scope plus allowed parents, and add a project isolation flag (nothing in from broader scopes, nothing out to them). Space memory applies only to Space turns authorised by a Control-signed Space decision and fails closed; later add an agent scope with a notes document per named agent and a Memory tab on the agents page.
whyItMatters: Business users mix clients and projects, and scoped memory prevents cross-project leakage while honouring the rule that Space access never widens an owner-plane ACL. A per-agent memory keeps personal memory clean and fits the agents-that-work-for-you-over-time direction of the agent pages.

referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Scoped memory: 5 of 12 (common). Named persistent agents: 4 of 12 (differentiator).
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: ChatGPT project-only memory defines the isolation contract: no outside memory comes in, nothing goes out, shared projects are always isolated and enterprise projects always contained; the project summary is regenerated from that project's chats only. Antigravity adds typed scopes with activation triggers and globs. Cursor gives an agent principal a small home store whose SELF.md is injected (tag-escaped) into each run and which the agent can edit, with a Memory tab listing files and source labels in Codex.

title: Enterprise compliance posture: retention windows and legal hold, data-use disclosure, regime tags, sharing policy, telemetry scrub, signed releases
summary: Add a Control Plane retention policy per org and surface with a legal-hold flag that a session-core sweeper obeys (dry-run and audited), propagating deletes to Data Plane indexes and derived memory, and finish Temporary chat once ZDR is attested. Show each provider's training and data-use posture in the model picker from capability-core provider metadata, generalise the ZDR feature-gate pattern into org regime tags in the Control-signed posture, design share links with an org-only default, an admin policy key and a ZDR refusal, scrub telemetry through a typed event registry at the OTel exporter, and build and sign a release artifact in CI with SHA-pinned actions and cargo-deny/govulncheck gates.
whyItMatters: Enterprises require retention windows and legal hold before deploying chat broadly, and a signed reproducible release is a prerequisite for credible security claims to enterprise buyers. Most pieces reuse designs Verevon already has (ZDR gate matrix, erasure consumers, privacy-tier routing, hash-only security events).

Lockfiles with exact pins, CI actions by SHA, minimum release age, signed artifacts with rollback.

title: Loop guard, durable org hooks and universal tool-output handles in both loops
summary: (1) A LoopGuard in mp-contracts used by both loops: a rolling window of (tool, args hash, result class) with an escalating reminder at 3, 5 and 8 identical failing calls, a stop with a typed loop_detected end reason, a repetition detector for streamed text (code-fence aware) and bounded retry on empty or length-stopped responses. (2) Persist org and Space hook rules in capability-core and pass hook_context into Do runs, which today receive none; handlers stay declarative rules plus HTTP webhooks (no shell) and hooks may only narrow authority. (3) Generalise ToolResultHandle from MCP results to every built-in tool result above a token threshold (fetch_url, knowledge, provider actions), run-scoped and never stored on ZDR turns.
whyItMatters: A stuck run that keeps repeating a failing call wastes tokens and is exactly what users describe as "it keeps doing the same thing". Hooks let org admins enforce policy (for example block mail outside the domain) without code changes, and result handles protect the context window in Do runs that read large documents. All three are small wiring jobs on existing primitives.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Hermes (side-effect-free loop controller for repeat, cycle and no-progress detection with stop gates) for the guard; Cursor (generic and tool-specific pre/post hooks) for hooks; DeepSeek (private spill files with opaque locators inside a shared token budget) for output handles
others: Antigravity (hook JSON contract with step injection)
Codex (command, MCP-tool and agent hook handlers)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: loop hygiene 3 of 12 (differentiator); hooks 3 of 12 (differentiator); output spill 3 of 12 (differentiator)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Guard: rolling window of (tool, args hash, result class); on N identical failing calls or no new information inject an escalating reminder, then stop with a loop reason. Hooks: registry {event, matcher, handler(command|http|prompt), timeout}; pre-hooks return allow|deny|ask plus optional rewritten input and context; durable store with per-org admin rules. Spill: if output exceeds max_inline_tokens store the full text as a run-scoped blob and return {preview_head, marker, preview_tail, handle, size}; a read tool fetches ranges; blobs expire with the run.

title: Public, versioned Agent API with origin-tagged runs as the one entry for every surface (SPA, API keys, schedules, mail, later channels)
summary: Expose a versioned /v1/agent API on model-gateway (create run, stream, resume, cancel, answer an interaction) behind Control-issued API keys exchanged for audience-bound delegated bearers, generate an SDK from the same contract, and make every run carry an origin and parent id (chat, console, api, schedule, mail, channel, subagent). Route scheduled and mail-triggered runs through the same governed pipeline, and treat future Channel Plane adapters (Teams, Slack) and a thin CLI as clients of this API.
whyItMatters: Enterprise customers and internal surfaces (Office add-ins, mail tasks, cron) can reuse the governed Do-mode pipeline instead of re-implementing it, and agents reachable from Teams or Slack raise daily use. Today Model Plane has one real front door, the SPA through the BFF, plus a hollow scheduled path.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex (one runtime, many thin surfaces); Manus (everything is a task with an id and URL)
others: Hermes Agent (messaging gateway with about 25 adapters)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: C-001: 6 of 12 (table-stakes). C-037: 3 of 12 (differentiator). C-038: 1 of 12 (unique)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Codex: one Rust binary exposes exec, review, resume and fork by id, queue, sandbox, execpolicy and an app-server daemon, so each surface is a thin client of the same runtime. Manus: a task.* API where chats, API tasks, schedules and sub-tasks are all tasks with a task_url. Hermes: channel adapters are plugins that connect, normalise, authorise, resolve a canonical session key (agent:{ns}:{platform}:{chat_type}:{chat_id}), queue busy sessions and stream replies.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: SRC: the gateway already serves a rich /v1 surface (invoke, stream, resume, runs, orchestration, tasks, cron) but only the BFF consumes it; there is no public Agent API, SDK, CLI or OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Threads carry a stored origin and system runs are listed, but a scheduled step is a single no-tool 1,024-token call with a receipt and no result delivery, and the daily-brief route has no SPA caller. auth-core has an optional API-key plugin (API_KEY_ENABLED) and a model-plane token controller that mints audience-bound RS256 bearers, so key-to-bearer exchange is feasible. The Channel Plane is docs-only and bridge-core is scaffolding.

approachOriginal: (1) Versioned /v1/agent routes in model-gateway that wrap the existing managed-run start, events, resume, cancel, plan-approval and interaction answers, with an OpenAPI spec generated from the Rust types (shares tooling with R-t3-13-07) and a generated SDK. (2) API keys from auth-core exchanged at the edge for audience-bound delegated bearers; the API must never bypass the BFF's bearer minting, ZDR propagation or per-org rate limits. (3) Extend the thread and run origin enum (api, schedule, mail, channel, subagent) and parent run id; run ScheduledRunSupervision through the full governed Do-mode loop with an unattended identity and deliver results to the thread plus notification-core (agent-runtime item R-t3-04-05 owns the loop semantics). (4) Later: stand up the Channel Plane with a Teams then Slack adapter calling this API, with per-channel identity mapping through Control, and a thin CLI.
planeOwner: Model Plane (model-gateway); Control Plane for keys; Channel Plane (not yet built) for adapters
risks: Widening the edge enlarges attack surface; unattended runs need always-ask or pre-approved plans; channel identity linking and per-platform data residency; the Channel Plane does not exist yet.

verevon.exactGap: SRC: model-gateway already serves the run lifecycle (invoke, stream, resume, cancel, queue, plan-approval, run events, runs list, cron) and an OpenAPI spec with generated TypeScript and Python SDKs exists, but only the BFF consumes it: the BFF authenticates by session cookie only, auth-core's API-key plugin (API_KEY_ENABLED, orpc verifyApiKey) has no consumer that exchanges a key for a model-gateway bearer, and there is no /v1/agent surface, CLI or OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Thread origin is a closed six-value CHECK list (chat, space, agent_run, support, system, mail_task; session-core grpc.rs THREAD_ORIGINS, migrations 0034/0041) with no api/schedule/channel/subagent value, the mail-task pipeline is wired to None in gateway config.rs:269 (every call answers 503), and a scheduled step is one no-tool 1,024-token inference (execution-core grpc.rs:498-531) with no result delivery.

verevon.approachAdjustment: Do not expose /v1/agent directly on model-gateway: host the versioned public surface at the Frontend Plane gateway (or a thin API edge that reuses its normalization and instruction injection) and authenticate API keys there through auth-core verifyApiKey and a delegated-bearer exchange, or first move instruction-layer resolution server-side. title: Declarative provider registry and bring-your-own connections
summary: Turn provider registration from environment configuration into data: a ProviderProfile (wire protocol, base and models URL, auth kind, compat switches, retry and timeout budgets, residency, privacy tier) stored by inference-core, added through a schema-generated admin form, with model discovery that proposes entries without mutating config until saved and an admin overlay (custom model ids, hide, reorder, unverified capability overrides). Then generalise the ChatGPT-subscription pattern into BYO connections held by Integration Core (API key, cloud role or helper command for Bedrock, Vertex, Azure Foundry, or a customer gateway), referenced by opaque connection id, with per-connection routing so a user or org can hold several connections of one provider.
whyItMatters: Enterprise and sovereign customers can add their own gateway, on-prem endpoint or cloud tenancy without a Verevon release, and heavy users can bring their own keys. It also covers the local-model need in a form appropriate for a cloud product.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: hermes (hermes-architecture-and-surfaces-091, 41 overridable provider profiles); claude desktop (claude-product-ux-107, claude-runtime-architecture-072 for BYO cloud accounts and helper credentials with TTL)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: registry 5 of 12 (common); BYO 6 of 12 (table-stakes); multi-instance 1 of 12; curation 2 of 12
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: A ProviderProfile dataclass per provider with api mode, auth type, base and models URLs and error classification, overridable by a user profile of the same name; BYO credentials come from key, cloud role or a helper script with TTL and silent refresh, with health probes on save, and platform and customer credentials never fall back to each other. [SRC]

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: Providers come from environment configuration (INFERENCE_PROVIDER_ORDER plus fixed adapters). Only the user-owned ChatGPT subscription route exists as a connection; there is no admin-defined provider record, compat switches, discovery, add-provider UI, API-key BYOK, customer cloud account or customer gateway. Whether a user or org can hold several connections of one provider, and any per-org model visibility beyond the router-policy table, have no baseline record (unknown).

approachOriginal: inference-core: provider-profile table with secrets referenced, never stored; discovery calls GET /models; profiles flow into the same fallback chain, privacy-tier gate and metered decorator. Customer-declared profiles default to the lowest privacy tier and no ZDR claim until attested. Integration Core: new credential kinds and short-lived token minting per call; Model Plane receives only an opaque connection id. cost-core: customer-billed flag. Frontend Plane: schema-annotated settings form. Phase 1 registry plus curation, phase 2 BYO.
risks: Unverified endpoints can claim residency or ZDR they do not have; customer endpoints may log prompts; confusing which account paid (show the connection on the served-by line); wrong capability overrides cause failures (mark unverified and log).

verevon.exactGap: SRC: provider registration is environment-only (inference-core config.rs from_env: INFERENCE_PROVIDER_ORDER plus fixed Anthropic, OpenAI-compatible base URL, Azure OpenAI, Azure Foundry Anthropic, Azure Cohere and ChatGPT-subscription adapters; ZDR attestation is an evidence-bound env block in provider/zdr.rs), and no Bedrock, Vertex, Gemini, Mistral or Ollama adapter exists. The only per-user connection is the ChatGPT-subscription route where Integration Core owns auth, inference-core receives an opaque subscription_connection_id, and a connection-level ZDR assessment runs at connect time; there is no provider-profile table, model discovery, compat switches, admin overlay, API-key BYOK or customer-gateway route. The only DB-backed precedent is the routing-policy JSONB singleton in session-core that inference-core polls (policy_client.rs).

cost-core metering decorator and the intent-layer fallback chain
verevon.constraints: Model Plane must not store provider secrets: reference an opaque connection id held by Integration Core (existing pattern). A customer-declared provider must default to the lowest privacy tier with no ZDR or residency claim; ZDR today requires an attestation with resource id, approval reference, effective and review-by dates and a digest, and global residency opt-ins are deny-by-default flags, so an admin form must not be able to type 'zdr: true'. Customer-billed routes need cost-core attribution and the served-by line must name the connection. Entitlement ownership between Control and Model Plane is an open decision (ADR dependency).
verevon.approachAdjustment: Phase it differently: (1) an admin overlay over the env-defined providers (hide, reorder, custom model ids), stored in session-core like the routing-policy singleton; (2) one new OpenAI-compatible customer-gateway profile with a secret reference and lowest privacy tier; (3) cloud-role BYO (Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry) last. Do not start with a generic registry that replaces env wiring: ZDR and residency attestation and provider-specific adapters (the Anthropic cache planner, Azure deployment names) cannot be expressed as compat switches. Schema-generated admin form is optional polish.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged for the full registry plus BYO; phase 1 overlay alone is M.
verevon.verdictReason: The capability is genuinely absent beyond the single subscription connection, so it stays, but the approach should start from an overlay on existing providers and preserve evidence-bound ZDR and residency rather than introduce a generic registry.

title: UI quality gates: remove Norwegian-only controls and enforce i18n and design tokens in CI
summary: Route the remaining Norwegian-only strings (approval buttons, plan rung labels, tool status words, trace copy) through i18n.tr, then add CI gates so they cannot come back: an ESLint rule against bare string literals in JSX under features/chat and features/agents, a dictionary-parity test, and a raw-colour ban outside tokens for new files. Write the per-surface state checklist (empty, loading, reconnecting, degraded, exhausted, error) into the design doc, and move toward namespace catalogs instead of inline tr(no, en) pairs so a third locale is feasible.
whyItMatters: Language leaks in the most important controls (approvals) are visible to every English user and to screen readers. A fast-growing SolidJS UI with a roughly 16k-line global.css needs automated guards to stay consistent across chat, agents and Spaces, and the Nordic market makes a clean Norwegian, English and later Swedish or Danish setup a real differentiator.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: DeepSeek (typed dictionaries, a gate against hard-coded copy, a parity test; semantic-token specs) plus Hermes Agent (layered locale packs, 34 KB DESIGN.md with a state checklist)
others: Claude desktop (34k ICU strings in 11 locales)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: i18n: 7 of 12 (table-stakes); design contract and token enforcement: 4 of 12 (common).
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Message keys in typed catalogs per feature namespace with ICU plural/select; a CI script fails on string literals in JSX outside the i18n call; a parity test asserts every key exists in every locale; typed failure causes select localised guidance. Tokens in three layers (scale, semantic alias, component) with a lint gate rejecting raw colours and literal spacing in feature code, one primitives catalog, and motion tokens with reduced-motion fallbacks.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: Norwegian and English are handled with inline i18n.tr(no, en) pairs, and several controls are Norwegian-only (the Godkjenn and Avvis approval buttons were verified as bare literals); there is no gate or parity test and only two locales. eslint.config.js (116 lines) has a no-restricted-syntax block (a fabricated-security-posture rule) but no raw-colour or JSX-string rule that I found; a single primitives catalog was not located. The design spec is marked stale against code.

approachOriginal: Frontend Plane: fix the leaks first. Then extend the existing no-restricted-syntax array in eslint.config.js (a second key would replace the existing A8 rule, per the comment in that file) with a JSX bare-literal selector scoped to features/chat and features/agents, add a Vitest parity test over the dictionaries, and add a stylelint or ESLint raw-colour rule for new files only (legacy global.css is too large for a big-bang gate). Add the state checklist and motion tokens to the design doc. Introduce namespace catalogs gradually, starting with approvals and tool status.
risks: Gate noise on legacy CSS and inline pairs, so scope new rules to new or touched files. Inline tr(no, en) pairs make a third locale costly until migrated. Needs verification of the token-gate half (check for an existing primitives kit under src/shared/ui).

verevon.exactGap: Confirmed bare or single-language literals in the most important controls: Godkjenn and Avvis approval buttons (ChatMessages.tsx:1917,1924), plan approve button (2523), rung labels (2538-2542), Tenker (3672), Last ned (ChatArtifactPanel.tsx:397,581), Stopp svar (ChatPage.tsx:947), run receipt labels and effect names (ChatPanels.tsx:1285-1306) and English-only Pause fleet (FleetRunConsole.tsx:155), while roughly 984 other strings in chat and agents use i18n.tr. eslint.config.js has one no-restricted-syntax array (fabricated-posture plus web-speech selectors, lines 93-108) and no JSX-literal or raw-colour rule, and no stylelint exists. The dictionaries en.ts and no.ts are about 40 lines each and en.ts documents inline tr(no, en) as the preferred pattern, so a parity test and namespace catalogs would add little.
reuse: eslint.config.js no-restricted-syntax array and the existing pnpm verify step that CI already runs (verevonv3-ci.yml)
useI18n().tr(no, en) pairs already used about 984 times in chat and agents
The AgentRunConsole approve control, which already uses an i18n.tr pair, as the model for the fix
shared/ui primitives (Button, Badge, MetricCard) and shared/ui/verevon (20 files)
node:test contract-test pattern in apps/gateway/scripts/*.test.mjs for repo-level text gates
verevon.constraints: Frontend Plane only; no plane, ZDR or Space-authority conflict. The one engineering constraint is ESLint flat config: a second block that matches the same files and sets no-restricted-syntax replaces the first, as the comment at eslint.config.js:104-105 warns.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Fix the roughly 15 to 20 leaking sites first. Then add JSXText and JSXAttribute (title, aria-label, placeholder, alt) literal selectors in a second config block scoped to features/chat and features/agents that re-spreads the existing A8 and web-speech selectors; extending the existing array would apply the rule to all of src. Drop the dictionary-parity test and the namespace-catalog migration: inline tr(no, en) is the documented convention and gives parity at each call site, and en.ts holds one feature. Scope the raw-colour rule to features/chat only (about 1 hex literal) or use a baseline, because features/agents has about 537 hex literals in Chatbot Studio Tailwind classes. apps/verevon-web/DESIGN.md is the marketing-site spec, so the state checklist needs its own document. global.css is about 49k lines with about 389 custom properties, not 16k.
verevon.effortNote: Lowered from M: leak fixes plus one or two lint selectors plus a short checklist doc; the parity test and catalog migration are dropped.
verevon.verdictReason: The leaks are real and the lint gate is absent, but the parity test and namespace-catalog parts contradict the documented inline-pair convention and have little to check, and the raw-colour gate needs scoping; reword to a small leak-fix plus JSX-literal gate.

title: Contract and architecture guardrails in CI: generated SPA types from Rust, plane-boundary and logging gates, and a size ratchet
summary: Generate TypeScript types for SSE payloads and BFF JSON from the Rust contracts (ts-rs or schemars into json-schema-to-ts, or from proto) with a CI diff failure, and add a test-mode payload validator in the SPA stream client that rejects unknown keys. Add syntax-aware fitness gates: no cross-plane DB access, no raw user content in logs, and a baselined file and function size ratchet whose enforcement level is read from the base branch.
whyItMatters: It removes the recurring class of bug where the backend emits an event the SPA silently drops, and it turns the plane-ownership and ZDR rules, which are enforced today by review and by docs that go stale, into durable checks that still hold when AI agents write most of the code.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Hermes Agent (schema codegen); DeepSeek harness (AST fitness gates)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Hermes: one Pydantic model per method, server request and event; a generator renders TypeScript types and an OpenRPC document; extra keys are rejected and test isolation raises ContractViolation on a mismatched payload. DeepSeek: AST-based repository checks that cannot be dodged by renamed imports, with SHA-256 baselines for retiring legacy violations; Hermes reads the ratchet level from main so a PR cannot relax its own check.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: SRC: CI guards SSE event-name taxonomy freshness, vendored contract goldens with sha256 pins, buf breaking changes, a resource-taxonomy lint and secret scanning. Not found: generated SPA payload types (chat-client.ts is hand-written; no ts-rs, specta, schemars or utoipa in the verevonv3 manifests), an automated check of the no-cross-plane-DB-access rule, a complexity ratchet (agent.rs is 13,521 lines, sse.rs 13,325 and http_routes.rs 11,681) or a stale-doc gate; the Model Plane CI job runs fmt, check and tests only.

approachOriginal: Types: derive schemars or ts-rs on the SSE event and BFF DTO structs in model-gateway and the verevonv3 gateway, emit committed .ts files under src/shared/api/generated, fail CI on diff, and add an assert-on-unknown-keys validator used in tests and dev builds of the SSE parser. Fitness: add a syn and go/ast based job that scans each service's DB URLs and migrations for foreign schemas, a lint gate that forbids logging prompt, message and tool-result fields (pairs with R-t3-13-09), a file and function size ratchet baselined by hash with the level read from the base branch, and a doc-freshness check tied to STALE_DOC_DELETION_REGISTER.md. This ratchet is also the answer to the oversized loop functions; do not add a contributor-registry abstraction for a single implementation (ledger.md:1358 rule).
planeOwner: Frontend Plane (types) and Support Plane (CI gates)

title: Multi-replica-safe run control: shared cancel, queued-input, plan-mode and turn state, durable send receipts and an editable message queue
summary: Move process-local run control in model-gateway (cancel flags, queued input, plan-mode flags, team workers, the chat-turn map, hook and command registries) behind run-id-keyed shared state in Redis/Dragonfly with NATS fan-out, and make duplicate-send protection durable using session-core receipts. whyItMatters: A model-gateway restart or a replica move currently loses in-flight cancels, queued messages and plan state; the stream buffer is in memory unless REDIS_URL is set.
